dependency: Preferred operating dependency: continuous 6 W base heating, kept on whenever obscuration returns, is treated as necessary for readable viewing throughout minutes 5 through 20. ATT breaks it by setting the pad to 0 W before the probe and keeping it at 0 W throughout every attack condition; fan remains off. Proposed passive moisture control must succeed without any heating restoration. The stipulated O2 early improvement supports a transient association with heating, not its necessity for the whole interval; O2 also fails the 90% readability target.

predictions.account: Hypothesis A: vapor supply is a dominant cause of late obscuration, and passive moisture removal can substitute for continuous heating.
predictions.result: With 50 mL initial tray water and the same damp sample, the proposed 0 W plus desiccant condition should have more readable cells and a smaller late humidity rise than 0 W alone. If passive removal is sufficient, at least 90 cells will remain readable at every assessed time from minute 5 through minute 20 while the sample stays below 35 C. A readability improvement below that threshold would be partial support only. Reduced tray mass loss is not required: desiccant can capture vapor after evaporation.
predictions.when: Hypothetical three-probe sequence, each after a five-minute reset to the stated initial quantities and temperatures: repeat 6 W/fan-off as a reference; change only power to 0 W for an unheated comparison; then retain 0 W/fan-off and introduce only 20 g fresh desiccant in the second removable tray, positioned outside the visible grid and without altering the viewing surface. End each probe by minute 20, record the exact placement and timing, and remove the added interface within two minutes. Score fixed images at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 minutes and the intervening one-minute images; log temperatures and humidity and weigh tray water and sample before and after. Reference heating is a control, not part of the proposed surviving solution.

predictions.account: Hypothesis B: warming the lid or another heat-dependent temperature distribution is necessary for target readability under these conditions; reducing vapor supply at 0 W is insufficient.
predictions.result: Both 0 W conditions should fail to maintain at least 90 readable cells throughout minutes 5 through 20, even if the desiccant condition lowers measured humidity. Early readability should track measured lid temperature more closely than the desiccant-induced humidity change. Failure with one desiccant amount would not establish universal heating necessity because placement, capacity and local humidity remain uncertain.
predictions.when: Apply the same proposed three-probe sequence and assessment times. Compare measured inner-lid temperature, humidity and readability across the unheated conditions and the 6 W reference. A comparable lid temperature with distinctly improved unheated readability would count against this strong necessity account; retain uncertainty because a single humidity sensor and temperature probes do not measure local vapor or condensation flux.

predictions.account: Hypothesis C: airflow distribution or local vapor delivery dominates the fan anomaly rather than bulk center-air temperature alone.
predictions.result: An optional fourth probe, retaining 0 W and the same desiccant placement but changing only fan setting from off to 60% at the marked orientation, could worsen late readability despite lower center-air temperature. That result would be consistent with local transport, while improved readability would challenge this direction of prediction. Neither result would directly identify transport or condensation flux.
predictions.when: Only if the first three hypothetical probes can be completed within their limits, perform this fourth and final probe after its five-minute reset, ending by minute 20 and using the same images, mass measurements and sensor logs. Stop immediately at a sample temperature of 35 C or pad surface temperature of 42 C; any limit crossing is a stopped probe, never success.

surviving_outcome: The valued outcome survives as the test criterion after removing continuous heating: at least 90% of the reference grid readable throughout minutes 5 through 20 with the damp sample below 35 C. A proposed unheated passive-moisture condition is a hypothesis, not an observed successful future. No supplied condition has demonstrated the full outcome: O5 reports 14% obscuration at minute 20 with 6 W after removing tray water, so it both misses the target and changes inventory. A useful surviving partial outcome would be measured improvement in readability at 0 W with its actual duration and temperature limits stated. No probes have been performed here and no real equipment or sample benefit is claimed.
unknowns: The stipulated observations do not establish whether vapor supply, lid temperature, airflow distribution or their interaction controls late obscuration; vapor-transfer links remain unobserved.
It is unknown whether the fresh desiccant capacity and placement can keep local lid humidity low enough for the entire target interval; a single humidity sensor does not resolve local gradients.

Before any proposed probe, confirm that the second tray and desiccant can be positioned without reducing visible grid area and removed within two minutes; if infeasible, omit that condition and report only the available partial comparison.
The 0 W attack must retain the initial 50 mL tray water and same damp sample; it cannot borrow O5 as evidence of success or silently remove water inventory.
Sparse images can miss intervening obscuration; inspect all available one-minute images and explicitly bound any claim between observations.
Stopping at a temperature limit or before minute 20 yields only a bounded partial result; no more than four probes are proposed and none may exceed 25 minutes after reset.
The fictional traces supply no real-system durability, contamination, performance or causal mechanism evidence; predicted substitutions and mechanisms remain hypotheses.
